headline: RON95 Quota Cut, April to August 2026: The 90% 'Unaffected' Figure Had No Published Basis
context: The monthly subsidised RON95 quota under BUDI95 fell from 300 to 200 litres on 1 April 2026, a cut MOF called temporary, and returned to 300 litres on 1 September. MOF said nearly 90% of users stayed under 200 litres but published no method.

cards.big: From 1 April 2026, RON95 stayed at RM1.99 only for the first 200 litres. MOF said nearly 90% of users would not be affected.
cards.sub: MOF gave no methodology or sample period for the figure and called the cut temporary. The quota returned to 300 litres on 1 September 2026.

cards.big: Above-quota RON95 sold at the weekly unsubsidised price from 1 April. The week of 16-22 April listed RM4.02 versus the subsidised RM1.99.
cards.sub: That gap is about 102% per litre. RM3.87 applied from 26 March to 8 April and from 23 to 29 April, a 94% gap.

cards.big: Indonesia's earlier subsidy cuts ran with direct cash assistance such as BLT BBM. Malaysia kept STR and SARA but added no dedicated BUDI95 transfer.
cards.sub: Each country's quota design, transfer and timing differ; the comparison is directional.

cards.big: E-hailing operators kept a separate 800-litre monthly ceiling. MOF published no usage spread showing which other users cross 200 litres.
cards.sub: The quota cut took effect four days after the Aidilfitri festive price-control scheme for goods ended on 28 March.

cards.big: The question is not whether 90% escaped the cut. It is whether even a temporary cut can rest on a number published without its working.
A quota cut without published targeting methodology, a transitional package or an alternatives plan rests on assertion. Show the arithmetic before the price changes.
